questions.q: How does trajectory tracking differ from path following?
options: It doesn't; they are synonyms in control theory
A trajectory can only be straight
You also have to be at the point on time
A path is defined only by splines
questions.explain: A trajectory is a path with time; it matters for formations and synchronized maneuvers.

questions.q: Lateral acceleration in the pure pursuit law?
options: a = V² / L with no angle
questions.explain: The curvature of the arc to the lookahead point is κ = 2 sin α / L, a = V²κ.

questions.q: What does a lookahead distance L that is too short cause?
options: Slow, smooth convergence onto the path line
questions.explain: Small L — sharp commands, overshoot; large L — slow, and corners get cut.

questions.q: L1 at V = 18 m/s, NAVL1_PERIOD = 17, NAVL1_DAMPING = 0.75?
What's wrong with a trapezoidal profile for a copter?
options: It is noticeably slower than any S-curve
It doesn't work in AUTO mode
questions.explain: Jerk is infinite: jerking, swinging of the payload and camera.

questions.q: What does the S-curve pay for smoothness in the 50 m example?
options: A 2 m overshoot at the end
questions.explain: Ramping acceleration with limited jerk adds time: 7.5 s versus 7.0.

questions.q: Why is it snap specifically that is minimized for a quadcopter?
options: Motor torques are tied to snap
Snap is the second derivative, so it's easier to compute
questions.explain: Thrust ~ acceleration, angular rate ~ jerk, torques ~ snap (the fourth derivative).

questions.q: Why does the companion send velocity and acceleration together with position?
questions.explain: Feedforward: the position controller only catches up with the residual error.
